guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our slight lean toward Wake Forest is less about its unbeaten start and more about an offense that has avoided drive-killing mistakes. We have seen Wake Forest play two games without a turnover, while Gio Lopez produced 575 passing yards, four passing touchdowns and another 98 yards on the ground. Carlos Hernandez also supplied 253 receiving yards. We view that production as useful context rather than proof, but it helps explain why our numbers give Wake Forest a chance to remain competitive.

The more important counterweight is Louisville’s defense. Our efficiency numbers grade Louisville better than Wake Forest’s offense against both the pass and the run, with an even stronger advantage in preventing scoring opportunities. That matters because Wake Forest’s early production has benefited from clean football; if Louisville disrupts that efficiency, the underdog’s margin for error narrows quickly.

We also have reservations about Wake Forest’s defense after Purdue produced a 329-yard passer and a 114-yard, three-touchdown rusher. We are not treating one game as a definitive forecast, but it reinforces the case for Louisville creating separation. For us, the competing signals leave our view too close to the market to justify a wager at the available price.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Lopez and the Wake Forest passing game against Louisville’s pass defense. Lopez’s ability to contribute through the air and on the ground gives Wake Forest a way to extend possessions, while Hernandez has already emerged as a productive target. Our matchup numbers still favor Louisville’s defense, so the question is whether Wake Forest can maintain its early ball security and create enough successful passing downs to keep the game within range.

recent_game.fact: Wake Forest defeated Purdue 38-36 in double overtime on Sept. 12, 2026, improving to 2-0.
On fourth-and-15 in the second overtime against Purdue, Gio Lopez completed a 15-yard pass to Carlos Hernandez; Lopez then scored the tying touchdown and the winning two-point conversion.
Wake Forest committed no turnovers against Purdue.
Purdue quarterback Ryan Browne passed for 329 yards, while running back Fame Ijeboi rushed 27 times for 114 yards and three touchdowns against Wake Forest.

opponent_notes.fact: Wake Forest is scheduled to play at Louisville on Sept. 26, 2026 at L&N Stadium; the schedule lists Louisville with a 1-1 record.

quarterback.fact: Starting quarterback Gio Lopez completed 16 of 27 passes for 225 yards and one touchdown against Purdue and added 59 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns.
Through two games, Lopez was 37-of-59 passing for 575 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions, with 98 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns.
Lopez transferred to Wake Forest from North Carolina after starting 11 games there in 2025; he previously played at South Alabama under current Wake Forest offensive coordinator Rob Ezell.
The unofficial depth chart lists redshirt freshman Steele Pizzella as Lopez's backup.

offensive_personnel.fact: Center Will Way, a January transfer from Weber State, was voted one of Wake Forest's six captains and is listed as the starting center on the unofficial depth chart.
Wake Forest's unofficial projected offensive line is Tolu Olajide at left tackle, Clinton Richard at left guard, Will Way at center, Ryan Berger at right guard and Aidan Martin at right tackle.
Carlos Hernandez had six receptions for 88 yards against Purdue and has 253 receiving yards through two games.
Running back Ty Clark III recorded his first career 100-yard game with 105 yards against Akron and scored a rushing touchdown against Purdue.
The unofficial depth chart lists Ty Clark III as the starting running back, with Florida transfer KD Daniels and freshmen Deuce Lawrence and Jamar Searcy behind him.
Wide receiver Antonio Meeks, listed as a starter on the unofficial depth chart, previously played at Louisville.

defensive_personnel.fact: Wake Forest's unofficial projected defensive front lists Langston Hardy and Gabe Kirschke at defensive end, Dallas Afalava at defensive tackle and Zach Lohavichan at nose guard.

The unofficial depth chart lists Frank Cusano and Aiden Hall at linebacker, Braylon Johnson at STAR, Deuce Blades II and Ashaad Williams at cornerback, Rushaun Tongue at free safety and Davaughn Patterson at strong safety.
Linebacker Aiden Hall recorded a career-high 73 tackles, eight tackles for loss and three passes defensed as a starter in 2025.
Vincent Firenze averaged 10 tackles and 5.5 solo tackles per game through Wake Forest's first two games.

coaching_changes.fact: Dyrell Roberts joined Wake Forest as wide receivers coach in 2026 after coaching East Carolina's wide receivers from 2023 through 2025.

Rob Ezell is Wake Forest's offensive coordinator, Dan Enos is co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, Scottie Hazelton is defensive coordinator, and Freddie Banks is co-defensive coordinator and safeties coach.

offensive_context.fact: Through two games, Wake Forest averaged 38.0 points, 485.0 total yards, 290.5 passing yards and 194.5 rushing yards per game.
Wake Forest converted 12 of 26 third downs and all three fourth-down attempts through its first two games.
Wake Forest had not committed a turnover through two games and had thrown no interceptions or lost any fumbles.

defensive_context.fact: Through two games, Wake Forest allowed 26.0 points and 380.0 total yards per game, including 242.5 passing yards and 137.5 rushing yards per game.
Wake Forest recorded five sacks and 15 tackles for loss through its first two games.
Wake Forest forced one turnover through two games, a fumble recovery by Rushaun Tongue against Akron, and had not recorded an interception.
Opponents converted 13 of 27 third downs against Wake Forest through two games.

special_teams.fact: Kicker Connor Calvert made six field goals through two games, averaging three per game with an 85.7 percent conversion rate.
The unofficial depth chart lists Koredell Bartley as the primary kickoff returner, Carlos Hernandez as the primary punt returner and freshman Ethan Hyams as the punter.
Wake Forest averaged 22.0 yards per punt return and 20.3 yards per kickoff return, with a 40.8-yard net punting average through two games.

series_context.fact: Wake Forest's schedule lists a 3-7 all-time record against Louisville.
The 2026 game is listed as only the fifth meeting between Wake Forest and Louisville since the 2006 ACC Championship Game.

other_relevant.fact: Wake Forest entered the Miami game 2-0 after wins over Akron and Purdue.
Wake Forest had scored 38 points in each of its first two games.
